m.chalisa.do1: Śrī Śanīścara Devajī, hear my cry with your ears. Lord, destroyer of countless obstacles, do not delay in doing me good.
m.chalisa.so1: Lord, I sing your praise with both hands joined. Remover of obstacles, son of Ravi, take me under your protection.
m.chalisa.cau1: Śanideva, I remember you; give me learning, wisdom and knowledge.
m.chalisa.cau2: I recount your many names, whatever I, of small understanding, know.
m.chalisa.cau3: I propitiate you as Antaka, Koṇa and Raudra; I proclaim to all the names Kṛṣṇa, Babhru and Śani.
m.chalisa.cau4: You are Piṅgala, Manda and Sauri, giver of happiness, knower of the good and ill of the whole world.
m.chalisa.cau5: Whoever chants your name daily, you free him from disease and sorrow.
m.chalisa.cau6: Under an adverse sign, demons, gods and men, serpents with Śeṣa, and the Vidyādharas,
m.chalisa.cau7: kings and paupers who are faring well, beasts, birds and forest creatures: of all of them
m.chalisa.cau8: the forests, forts, camps and armies, every village and whole cities: you bring them all to ruin.
m.chalisa.cau9: You cast obstacles into everyone's happiness; all grow distressed and fall into sorrow.
m.chalisa.cau10: Lord, this is my prayer to you: show me abundant mercy.
m.chalisa.cau11: Lord, for my good, do not dwell in an adverse sign; this is my only hope.
m.chalisa.cau12: Those who on Saturday give jaggery, black gram, sesame, barley, iron, grain, wealth and clothes
m.chalisa.cau13: become happy by giving these gifts. You are that Śani: hear this prayer of ours.
m.chalisa.cau14: Lord, show mercy to me, that millions of obstacles may perish in a moment.
m.chalisa.cau15: Lord, I bow to you with both hands joined; be merciful and hear my prayer.
m.chalisa.cau16: Sometimes at Prayāga, king of holy places, sometimes lovingly on the bank of the Sarayū,
m.chalisa.cau17: sometimes in the pure stream of the Sarasvatī, or somewhere in mountain hollows and caves,
m.chalisa.cau18: the yogis who meditate: in their meditation Śani becomes subtle.
m.chalisa.cau19: He is beyond reach; what praise can I give him? I bow, my head at his feet.
m.chalisa.cau20: Whoever turns back from abroad on a Saturday and comes to his own home
m.chalisa.cau21: stays happy, by Śanideva's name I swear it; the son of Ravi keeps him well protected.
m.chalisa.cau22: Those who go abroad on a Saturday do not come home, and suffer distress.
m.chalisa.cau23: Śani brings hardship on such a one, and he is as sorrowful at heart as one can be.
m.chalisa.cau24: To that same son of Ravi I, foolish and of little understanding, bow with joined hands.
m.chalisa.cau25: Brahmā is the maker of the world; Viṣṇu daily gives food to all.
m.chalisa.cau26: There is Śiva, bearer of the trident, foe of Tripura. These all-pervading gods are one form.
m.chalisa.cau27: As one, they ever hold Śani in mind; they bow to Śani with minds subdued.
m.chalisa.cau28: The man who reads this with heart and mind is freed from boundless suffering.
m.chalisa.cau29: Good sons are born to him, his wealth and offspring grow; Kali and Kāla stand before him with joined hands.
m.chalisa.cau30: His home stays ever filled with all things: cattle, family, kin and the rest.
m.chalisa.cau31: He enjoys pleasures of many kinds and every happiness, and at the end, leaving the world,
m.chalisa.cau32: attains liberation, the immortal state, brother, he who daily meditates on Śani with an even mind.
m.chalisa.cau33: Whoever recites the ten names of Śani in the morning, Śanīścara ever stays under his sway.
m.chalisa.cau34: Affliction from Śani never comes to whoever rises daily and meditates on him.
m.chalisa.cau35: Those who recite this Chālīsā gain happiness; the Lord of the world is witness.
m.chalisa.cau36: Whoever reads it every morning for forty days, Śani destroys his many sins.
m.chalisa.cau37: Such is the majesty of the son of Ravi, brother, that he destroys the darkness of delusion in the world.
m.chalisa.cau38: Whoever recites this will never lack happiness and wealth.
m.chalisa.cau39: Whoever meditates on him in his mind night and day, troubles of mind and body come nowhere near him.
m.chalisa.do2: Vimala has prepared this reading of Śanīścara Deva. Reading it for forty days, one crosses the ocean of worldly existence.
m.chalisa.do3: The hymn that Daśaratha sang, beholding Śani before him, that same hymn Lalitā has refined and written in sweet, fine language.
